claims.assertion: The driver cancelled this RydeX trip and the $6.61 cancellation fee was charged to my client, so the fee's validity is governed solely by NS-0's driver-cancellation/no-show branch (NS-1/NS-2).

The driver's own timeline record contradicts the 'I'm Here' prerequisite: one timeline entry shows a tap at 18:22:50 while another entry records that the driver never tapped 'I'm Here' (driver_pressed_here_at is null); the precondition in NS-1(i) is therefore not established on this record.

Even treating 18:22:50 as the tap, the driver was 41 m from the pickup point at the tap (F6) and stationary 41 m away from 18:22:30 to 18:26:40 (F3), which places him within the 200 m arrival radius used by the platform's own arrival logic; the NS-1(ii) location element is satisfied on the system record.

The driver was inside 200 m of the pickup for 5 min 15 s cumulatively before cancelling (F2) and stayed within 200 m for 3 min 50 s after the 18:22:50 tap (F6), while the platform recorded arrival at 18:21:00 and the cancellation 5 min 40 s later (F5); measured on the platform's own arrival record the wait exceeds the 3-minute threshold in NS-1(iii).

My client was responsive, not a no-show: she messaged at 18:24 asking for two more minutes and the driver cancelled at 18:26:40 having said he 'called twice'; the driver's refusal to grant a short grace period in heavy rain (18.5 mm) is not one of the two fee-charging situations the policy permits.
If the judge finds any NS-1 element unmet, NS-2 requires the full $6.61 to be refunded; the amount is verified by the fare record (F8) and NS-7 fixes the form of the refund as a voucher, not cash.

No safety element arises from the chat or the record: no threat keywords appear and the traffic record shows no incident near the route, so the case is decided on the fee rules alone rather than escalated.

weaknesses: The system records cut both ways: F2 (5 min 15 s within 200 m) and F5 (arrival 18:21:00, cancellation 5 min 40 s later) let the driver argue NS-1(i)-(iii) are all met, which would make the $6.61 fee stand under NS-1 and force no_action.

F6 fixes a 41 m standoff at the 18:22:50 tap and F3 shows the driver stationary 41 m away for 4 min 10 s; the driver can argue he did press 'I'm Here' and waited, so my reading of F7 as a null record is contested by the other side.

My own client's requests are unhelpful here: F11 shows she asked for '2 more minutes' only at 18:24, i.e. after the 18:21:00 recorded arrival, and F12/F13 show the driver says he called twice with no answer—there is no record of her picking up or approaching the vehicle.

Weather (F16, heavy rain) and the absence of incidents (F15) do not by themselves excuse a delay in boarding; NS-1 sets a 3-minute wait threshold and the policy contains no rain grace period, so the rain argument is sympathetic rather than binding.

My client's profile (F17) shows a prior upheld no-show dispute in the last 90 days, which the other side can use to suggest a pattern; under the rules profile facts cannot decide the case, and F18 shows the driver with a clean 90-day record, so no flag_account is available to us.

claims.assertion: The driver did press the arrival button and was physically at the pickup point: the platform recorded his arrival at 18:21:00, GPS shows him stationary only 41 m from the pickup from 18:22:30 to 18:26:40, and his closest approach was 38 m at 18:25:25, all well inside the 200 m arrival radius.

The driver waited far longer than the 3 minutes required: he was within 200 m of the pickup from 18:21:00 with 5 min 15 s cumulative presence inside the radius before cancellation, and he cancelled 5 min 40 s after the recorded arrival, i.e. 7 min 40 s after acceptance.

The rider confirmed by chat that she was still not at the pickup point and asked for extra time at 18:24, and never boarded; the driver cancelled at 18:26:40, more than 3 minutes after that message, so every NS-1 condition (arrival tap, GPS at pickup, waiting > 3 min) is satisfied and the $6.61 cancellation fee stands.

The driver's conduct is consistent and not an abuse of the cancellation/waiting button: he messaged the rider on arrival and cancelled for non-appearance after calling twice, and his account shows 317 trips in 90 days with 0 upheld disputes in the last 90 days, so no flag_account is warranted.

The weather at the time (heavy rain, thundery showers, 18.5 mm) explains heavy demand and short rider delays but does not create any published rule allowing a rider to extend a driver's waiting obligation past the 3-minute threshold; the fee therefore remains chargeable.

weaknesses: The timeline slice contains a contradicting record: F7 states the driver never tapped "I'm Here" (driver_pressed_here_at is null), while F6 says he tapped at 18:22:50 — the rider will argue NS-1(i) fails so the fee must be refunded under NS-2.

The rider's own message F11 (18:24) shows the delay was only "2 more minutes" from her, and the driver cancelled at 18:26:40, so the rider will argue he cut short a promise he had effectively been told about; she may also rely on her profile showing a prior upheld no-show dispute (F17) to appear credible.

No traffic incident evidence supports any excuse for the driver's timing (F15), and the speed band on Maxwell Road was only 20–29 km/h (F14), which the rider could cite as irrelevant to whether the waiting period was validly completed.
If the judge resolves the F6/F7 conflict in the rider's favour, the fee is fully refundable (NS-2) and may additionally attract a flag_account against the driver for the arrival-button discrepancy.

events.title: Proposed ruling: no_action (model confidence 0.78)
events.body:
This is a completed fare/NS dispute, not a safety case: the chat facts carry no threat content and the only safety-adjacent items are weather and traffic, so no escalation path applies [F12][F15][F16][SAFE-1]. Cancellation was made by the driver on a no-show basis, so the fee's validity runs solely through NS-0 into NS-1/NS-2 [F4][F8][NS-0]. The recorded cancellation fee is $6.61 and the trip is a RydeX (non-taxi) booking, so the amount at stake is fixed by the record rather than by any meter arithmetic; the trace's formula resolves to no refundable component (null amount) [F8][NS-0][NS-2].

NS-1(i) is established on the system record: the timeline shows the arrival tap at 18:22:50 at 41 m from the pickup point, corroborated by the recorded platform arrival at 18:21:00 [F6][F5][NS-1]. The null "driver_pressed_here_at" field in F7 is a data-layer artifact that conflicts with the affirmative timeline entries; system timeline records are the authoritative layer, and F6 plus F5 describe an actual, corroborated arrival tap, whereas F7 merely reports the absence of a value [F6][F7][F5][NS-1].

NS-1(ii) holds: the driver was 41 m from the pickup at the moment of the tap, inside the 200 m arrival radius, and his closest approach was 38 m [F6][F1][NS-1]. NS-1(iii) also holds: he remained continuously inside 200 m for 230 s after the tap, well over the 181 s required, having been cumulatively within 200 m for 5 min 15 s and cancelling 5 min 40 s after the recorded arrival [F6][F2][F5][NS-1][NS-3].

The rider's message at 18:24 asking for "2 more minutes" is a request for an extension, not a boarding, and the driver stayed stationary at the pickup until 18:26:40 without the rider reaching the vehicle; the policy publishes no rain grace period and sets the wait threshold at just over 3 minutes [F11][F3][F16][F4][NS-1]. Because all three NS-1 elements are satisfied, NS-2 is not triggered and the $6.61 fee stands; the driver's uncontradicted "called twice" statement is corroborative only and is not needed to carry the fee [F12][F13][F2][F3][F5][F6][NS-1][NS-2].

No account action is applied: the trace requires none, the driver's 90-day record shows zero upheld disputes, and the driver-side profile field is not itself a ground for flagging [F18][NS-2][RD-6].

what_would_change: Had the driver tapped I'm Here more than 200 m away, or left before 3 minutes, NS-2 would refund the fee in full.

claims.assertion: The driver cancelled this RydeX trip and the $6.61 cancellation fee was charged to my client, so the fee's validity is governed solely by NS-0's driver-cancellation/no-show branch (NS-1/NS-2).

The driver's own timeline record contradicts the 'I'm Here' prerequisite: one timeline entry shows a tap at 18:22:50 while another entry records that the driver never tapped 'I'm Here' (driver_pressed_here_at is null); the precondition in NS-1(i) is therefore not established on this record.

Even treating 18:22:50 as the tap, the driver was 41 m from the pickup point at the tap (F6) and stationary 41 m away from 18:22:30 to 18:26:40 (F3), which places him within the 200 m arrival radius used by the platform's own arrival logic; the NS-1(ii) location element is satisfied on the system record.

The driver was inside 200 m of the pickup for 5 min 15 s cumulatively before cancelling (F2) and stayed within 200 m for 3 min 50 s after the 18:22:50 tap (F6), while the platform recorded arrival at 18:21:00 and the cancellation 5 min 40 s later (F5); measured on the platform's own arrival record the wait exceeds the 3-minute threshold in NS-1(iii).

My client was responsive, not a no-show: she messaged at 18:24 asking for two more minutes and the driver cancelled at 18:26:40 having said he 'called twice'; the driver's refusal to grant a short grace period in heavy rain (18.5 mm) is not one of the two fee-charging situations the policy permits.
If the judge finds any NS-1 element unmet, NS-2 requires the full $6.61 to be refunded; the amount is verified by the fare record (F8) and NS-7 fixes the form of the refund as a voucher, not cash.

No safety element arises from the chat or the record: no threat keywords appear and the traffic record shows no incident near the route, so the case is decided on the fee rules alone rather than escalated.

weaknesses: The system records cut both ways: F2 (5 min 15 s within 200 m) and F5 (arrival 18:21:00, cancellation 5 min 40 s later) let the driver argue NS-1(i)-(iii) are all met, which would make the $6.61 fee stand under NS-1 and force no_action.

F6 fixes a 41 m standoff at the 18:22:50 tap and F3 shows the driver stationary 41 m away for 4 min 10 s; the driver can argue he did press 'I'm Here' and waited, so my reading of F7 as a null record is contested by the other side.

My own client's requests are unhelpful here: F11 shows she asked for '2 more minutes' only at 18:24, i.e. after the 18:21:00 recorded arrival, and F12/F13 show the driver says he called twice with no answer—there is no record of her picking up or approaching the vehicle.

Weather (F16, heavy rain) and the absence of incidents (F15) do not by themselves excuse a delay in boarding; NS-1 sets a 3-minute wait threshold and the policy contains no rain grace period, so the rain argument is sympathetic rather than binding.

My client's profile (F17) shows a prior upheld no-show dispute in the last 90 days, which the other side can use to suggest a pattern; under the rules profile facts cannot decide the case, and F18 shows the driver with a clean 90-day record, so no flag_account is available to us.

claims.assertion: The driver did press the arrival button and was physically at the pickup point: the platform recorded his arrival at 18:21:00, GPS shows him stationary only 41 m from the pickup from 18:22:30 to 18:26:40, and his closest approach was 38 m at 18:25:25, all well inside the 200 m arrival radius.

The driver waited far longer than the 3 minutes required: he was within 200 m of the pickup from 18:21:00 with 5 min 15 s cumulative presence inside the radius before cancellation, and he cancelled 5 min 40 s after the recorded arrival, i.e. 7 min 40 s after acceptance.

The rider confirmed by chat that she was still not at the pickup point and asked for extra time at 18:24, and never boarded; the driver cancelled at 18:26:40, more than 3 minutes after that message, so every NS-1 condition (arrival tap, GPS at pickup, waiting > 3 min) is satisfied and the $6.61 cancellation fee stands.

The driver's conduct is consistent and not an abuse of the cancellation/waiting button: he messaged the rider on arrival and cancelled for non-appearance after calling twice, and his account shows 317 trips in 90 days with 0 upheld disputes in the last 90 days, so no flag_account is warranted.

The weather at the time (heavy rain, thundery showers, 18.5 mm) explains heavy demand and short rider delays but does not create any published rule allowing a rider to extend a driver's waiting obligation past the 3-minute threshold; the fee therefore remains chargeable.

weaknesses: The timeline slice contains a contradicting record: F7 states the driver never tapped "I'm Here" (driver_pressed_here_at is null), while F6 says he tapped at 18:22:50 — the rider will argue NS-1(i) fails so the fee must be refunded under NS-2.

The rider's own message F11 (18:24) shows the delay was only "2 more minutes" from her, and the driver cancelled at 18:26:40, so the rider will argue he cut short a promise he had effectively been told about; she may also rely on her profile showing a prior upheld no-show dispute (F17) to appear credible.

No traffic incident evidence supports any excuse for the driver's timing (F15), and the speed band on Maxwell Road was only 20–29 km/h (F14), which the rider could cite as irrelevant to whether the waiting period was validly completed.
If the judge resolves the F6/F7 conflict in the rider's favour, the fee is fully refundable (NS-2) and may additionally attract a flag_account against the driver for the arrival-button discrepancy.

points.response: Geographic presence is not the disputed element — D1 only shows the driver was at the pickup (F1, F2, F3); it does not cure the fact that the record of the required arrival tap is self-contradictory, as F6 and F7 give two opposite accounts and NS-1(i) is satisfied only by a valid 'I'm Here'.

D2's 'more than 3 minutes' rests on the recorded arrival at 18:21:00 (F5), but the driver's own tap time is 18:22:50 (F6), and even on that later starting point the platform shows he stayed in the radius for 3 min 50 s (F6); the point therefore proves only that NS-1(ii) is met while NS-1(i) remains unresolved.

My client never disputed asking for time — her 18:24 message (F11) shows she was engaged and answering, not absent, and NS-1 charges the fee only where all three elements hold; the driver's assertion that he 'called twice' (F12, F13) is a statement to which no call record or system fact corresponds, so it cannot carry the fee under the rule that system records win over statements.

I do not seek a flag_account against the driver, so D4 is answered by withdrawing that point entirely; the driver's clean 90-day history (F18) is why my brief has no flag request, and it does not make the $6.61 payable.

I concede there is no published rain grace period extending the driver's waiting obligation (F16), and NS-1 sets a 3-minute threshold with no weather exception; the rain is context supporting why my client answered rather than attended immediately, not a standalone rule.
Accepted that the fee's validity turns on NS-1/NS-2, and on those clauses the fee stands: F4/F8 confirm a driver cancellation with $6.61 charged, and F2, F3, F5 and F6 supply each NS-1 element.

F7 is a null/superseded field record, while the affirmative timeline and GPS records show a real, corroborated arrival tap: F6 puts the tap at 18:22:50 with the driver 41 m from the pickup and F2/F3 confirm he was inside 200 m from 18:21:00 and stationary 41 m away from 18:22:30; the rider offers no system record showing the driver was absent or stationary elsewhere, so NS-1(i) is established on the record that the policy makes authoritative.
Agreed, and the rider's own concession on NS-1(ii) satisfies the location element of NS-1 in my client's favour.

Agreed as recorded: F5 puts arrival at 18:21:00 and cancellation 5 min 40 s later, F2 gives 5 min 15 s cumulative within 200 m and F6 gives 3 min 50 s inside 200 m after the tap, all exceeding the > 180 s requirement in NS-1(iii), so the fee is validly charged and the rider's refund claim fails.

A rider message asking for more time is not a boarding: F11 (18:24) shows she was still coming down and F3 shows the driver stationary at the pickup until 18:26:40 without her ever reaching the vehicle, and NS-1 sets a fixed > 3-minute wait with no grace period, so heavy rain (F16) and the rider's courtesy message do not defeat the fee; the driver's 18:26 message in F12 further shows two unanswered calls.
NS-2 is not triggered because NS-1(i)–(iii) are each met on the system records (F2, F3, F5, F6), so no $6.61 voucher is owed under NS-2 or NS-7.
Agreed — no safety element and no escalation; the case is decided under NS-0/NS-1 on the fee rules, which leaves the $6.61 charge standing.
I withdraw nothing but narrow D3's basis: the fee rests on the system records (F2, F3, F5, F6) rather than on the chat timing in F10–F12, since chat is only corroborative at NS-1.
